ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: Cutting off every stream is the middle of a recurring three-phrase set and also a direct claim about speech that permits no continuation or turning back.
EvidenceBody: Guizong Huitong, Shangfang Qiyue, Ruiyan Zhicai, and Rifang Shangzuo answer direct questions about the stream-cutting phrase with an iron mountain, a weeping woman, “Good,” and a crosswise staff.

Deshan Yuanming explicitly places it between covering heaven and earth and following the waves. Yuanwu Keqin uses it as the action of a solitary proclamation and as a capacity that surpasses present and past.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: A common image of stopping flows becomes a named public-interview category whose answer must itself demonstrate interruption rather than merely explain it.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: The phrase belongs to a three-part contrast in many cases; it must not absorb the distinct jobs of covering everything or following the waves.

ComparedThings: the same expression in questions, answers, comments, and verdicts
